source.version: Journal version of record, Batı Anadolu Eğitim Bilimleri Dergisi / Western Anatolia Journal of Educational Sciences, 2026, 17(1), 70-93; published 28 April 2026, as stated on PDF p. 1 (printed p. 70); DOI 10.51460/baebd.1757062.
source.title_on_document: ChatGPT Destekli Dönütlerin İlkokul Öğrencilerinin Yaratıcı Yazma Becerilerine Etkisi

supplement.where: Appendices Ek 1, Ek 2 and Ek 3, PDF pp. 22-24 (printed pp. 91-93). No separate external supplement is identified.
supplement.holds: Images of student texts from intervention weeks (Ek 1), student post-test texts (Ek 2), and example ChatGPT texts (Ek 3). They contain illustrative writing samples, not additional outcome statistics, standard errors or confidence intervals. The statistical results are in main-text Tables 5-8.

paper_design_summary: Third-grade pupils in two intact classes at a public school in Van completed creative-writing activities; class names were drawn from a bag, with the first class assigned to the experimental condition and the next to control (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Çalışma grubu). The experimental class received ChatGPT-generated example texts, peer feedback, teacher-guided comparison and rewriting over six weeks; the control class wrote and shared texts without the additional feedback (PDF pp. 9, 11-13, printed pp. 78, 80-82). The researcher scored individual pre-test and subsequent week-8 post-test stories; the results report 30 pupils analyzed in each arm, although a separate passage reports exclusions that are not reconciled with those counts (PDF pp. 11-12 and 15, printed pp. 80-81 and 84).

studies.label: Class-assigned creative-writing intervention and post-intervention writing assessment

assignment.what_was_assigned: Intact third-grade classes, not individual pupils. Names of the school's eight third-grade classes were put into a bag; the first drawn class was assigned to the experimental group and the next to control. The school was selected by convenience. Coding follows this explicit class-level lottery, despite the author describing the study as quasi-experimental. There is one class per arm.
assignment.quote: Okulda bulunan sekiz 3. Sınıf şubelerinin isimleri ayrı kâğıtlara yazılarak bir torbaya atılmış; ilk seçilen şube deney grubu, seçilen bir sonraki şube ise kontrol grubu olarak atanmıştır.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Çalışma grubu, paragraph after Table 1; author's quasi-experimental label: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 76), Araştırmanın modeli; between-class allocation with repeated pre/post assessment: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 81), Table 4.

arms.name: ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting
arms.description: One class wrote an initial story, shared it and received peer feedback, examined a ChatGPT-generated story on the same theme with the teacher, and rewrote its own work. The teacher also explained creative-writing techniques. Students did not use ChatGPT individually (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, intervention description). The reported analyzed count is from Tables 6-7, PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84).

arms.name: Writing practice without added feedback
arms.description: One class completed paper-and-pencil creative writing on the same weekly themes and shared texts with classmates, without teacher feedback or additional creative-writing instruction outside the usual lesson (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 81-82, Table 4 and intervention description). The reported analyzed count is from Tables 6-7, PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84).

participants.exclusions: Before the main creative-writing pre-test, a basic-writing screening exercise and teacher judgments led to exclusion of data from 4 experimental-group pupils and 5 control-group pupils with low writing skills (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Veri toplama süreci). The paper nevertheless reports 60 participants and N=30 in each arm in Tables 1 and 6-7 (PDF pp. 8 and 15, printed pp. 77 and 84). The form retains the explicitly reported analysis Ns. The paper does not reconcile exclusions with these counts or state the number of pupils at class assignment; no starting total or alternative analyzed total is inferred. This is not identified as an intention-to-treat analysis.
participants.who: Third-grade pupils at one public school in Van; the extended abstract specifies the İpekyolu district and the 2024-2025 academic year. School selection was by convenience. Only pupil participants are counted; teachers, the researcher and a separate feasibility-pilot class are not added.
participants.quote: Araştırmanın çalışma grubu, Van ilinde devlet okullarının birinde 3. sınıfta öğrenimine devam eden 60 öğrenciden oluşmaktadır.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 72), Extended Abstract, Method; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Çalışma grubu and Table 1; exclusions and feasibility pilot: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 80), Veri toplama süreci; analysis counts: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Tables 6-7.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, GPT-3.5, accessed through the OpenAI website, as reported (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT).
ai_tool.how_used: The teacher entered the writing theme through an electronic classroom board to obtain an example narrative; the class read and compared that example with student-written texts, received teacher/peer feedback and rewrote its texts. The model did not directly receive each pupil's draft for personalized editing, and pupils did not individually chat with it. Thus the delivered AI content is coded as supplied examples, although the paper calls the instructional process feedback (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81).

task.description: Narrative writing from supplied topics or word banks, using hypothetical situations, imaginary characters, word-bank stories and some collaborative classroom writing. The scored pre-test and post-test required individual narrative texts on different prompts. Weekly practice texts and ChatGPT examples are illustrated in the appendices, but no separate weekly creativity scores are reported (PDF pp. 10-12, printed pp. 79-81, Tables 3-4 and Veri toplama süreci; PDF pp. 22-24, Ek 1-3).
task.duration: Six intervention weeks, one day per week with three 40-minute lessons for the experimental class; eight weeks including preparation and the pre/post tests. The pre-test writing period was 40 minutes; a separate post-test duration is not stated (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Table 4).

outcomes.name: Creative Writing Products Evaluation Scale total score on the post-intervention story
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The researcher scored student-written stories with Kasap's (2019) Yaratıcı Yazma Ürünlerini Değerlendirme Ölçeği, a unidimensional 24-item scale with each item scored 1-5 and a total range of 24-120; sample Cronbach alpha is .88 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Veri toplama araçları; scoring by the researcher: PDF p. 11, printed p. 80). The researcher is the university-affiliated author (PDF p. 1, printed p. 70), so the measure is coded expert_raters; assessor blinding and inter-rater agreement are not reported. Performance bands are an alternative summary of this same score, not an additional outcome: low 24-48, medium 49-72, good 73-96, advanced 97-120 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, Table 2). PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), prose between Tables 6 and 7, reports experimental pre-test counts of 26 low, 3 medium and 1 good, and control pre-test counts of 26 low and 4 medium; experimental post-test counts are 7 low, 6 medium, 12 good and 5 advanced, and control post-test counts are 25 low and 5 medium. Pre/post paired tests and the post-test eta statistics also summarize this same outcome. No separate novelty, fluency, flexibility, elaboration or between-person diversity scores are reported. No outcome is explicitly designated primary.
outcomes.delay: The post-test is a later session in week 8, following the ChatGPT intervention in weeks 2-7; elapsed days since the last AI activity are not stated. Table 4 confines ChatGPT support to the intervention weeks and lists the same story-writing assessment for both groups at post-test. Coding after_ai/no AI follows this reported protocol; the text does not separately state a formal prohibition on AI during the test (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81, Veri toplama süreci and Table 4).

contrasts.treatment_arm: ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting
contrasts.reported: Post-test, Table 6: Deney N=30, mean=73,40, S=24,61; Kontrol N=30, mean=40,23, S=11,33; sd=58, t=6.705, p=.000. Post-test, Table 8: η=.771, η²=.594. Baseline, Table 6: Deney N=30, mean=34,23, S=14,56; Kontrol N=30, mean=35,66, S=10,82; sd=58, t=-.433, p=.667. Additional within-arm comparisons of this same outcome, Table 7: experimental pre/post N=30 at each time, means 34,23 and 73,40, S=14,56 and 24,61, sd=29, t=-7.887, p=.000; control pre/post N=30 at each time, means 35,66 and 40,23, S=10,82 and 11,31, sd=29, t=-8.238, p=.000. Table 7 prints control post-test S=11,31, whereas Table 6 prints 11,33. The prose on PDF p. 16 instead labels both paired tests t(30). All values and p=.000 are retained as printed; no effect size, standard error or interval is computed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Tables 6 and 7; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 85), Table 8 and opening paragraph. Table 7 is titled Shapiro-Wilk results but contains the paired-comparison N, mean, S, sd, t and p columns; analysis methods identify paired and independent t-tests on PDF p. 13 (printed p. 82), Verilerin analizi.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Not stated; the document does not identify a shared sample or a reanalysis of another paper.

company_involvement.description: No company involvement in authorship, funding or study conduct is reported. The author is affiliated with Van Yüzüncü Yıl University; OpenAI is named as the provider of the ChatGPT website used in the intervention, which alone is not coded as company involvement.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 70), author affiliation; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 78), ChatGPT.

eligibility.reason: The explicit lottery assigned intact classes to AI-supported writing instruction or no-AI writing practice: first drawn class experimental, next control (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Çalışma grubu). This supports a class-randomized field experiment under the codebook, despite the author's quasi-experimental label on PDF p. 7. The paper reports 60 pupils and analyzes N=30 per arm (PDF p. 8, Table 1; PDF p. 15, Tables 6-7), exceeding the people threshold; the unreconciled exclusion passage is recorded rather than used to invent an alternative count (PDF p. 11). Creativity is scored by the researcher on students' written stories (PDF pp. 8 and 11); the scored post-test follows the AI intervention (PDF p. 12, Table 4), so it answers after_ai. Core eligibility does not make the reported precision suitable for pooling: only one class is assigned to each arm, and the paper reports pupil-level t-tests without a class-cluster adjustment (PDF pp. 8, 13 and 15).

one_line_finding: After six weeks of ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting, the reported post-test creative-writing score was 73,40 (S=24,61; N=30) versus 40,23 (S=11,33; N=30) with writing practice alone, t(58)=6.705, p=.000 as printed (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Table 6); class clustering and bundled feedback limit attribution.
open_questions: How do the exclusions of 4 experimental and 5 control pupils relate to the analyzed N=30 per arm, and what were the pupil counts when classes were assigned? The paper does not reconcile these passages (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, versus PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).

Can inference appropriate to class assignment be supported? The lottery produces one class per arm, whereas reported t-tests use pupil-level degrees of freedom; no cluster adjustment or classroom-level precision is reported (PDF pp. 8, 13 and 15, printed pp. 77, 82 and 84).

Confirm that week-8 post-test stories were produced without access to ChatGPT examples or the intervention feedback/revision procedure. Table 4 and the data-collection description support after_ai coding, but do not expressly prohibit AI during testing (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81).

Resolve the control post-test SD discrepancy (11,33 in Table 6; 11,31 in Table 7), the paired-test df discrepancy (29 in Table 7; t(30) in the next-page prose), and the Shapiro-Wilk caption on the table of paired t-tests (PDF pp. 15-16, printed pp. 84-85).
notes: Screened on 2026-10-09. Locators use the 1-based PDF page, with journal page numbers in parentheses. The complete markdown was read in consecutive chunks through its end, including references and appendices; all recorded numerical results were checked against PDF text, and Tables 6-8 and the appendix images were also inspected visually. Outcome inventory: Tables 1-4 describe the sample, scale bands, tasks and schedule; Table 5 checks normality of the same creativity score; Tables 6-8 report the total creativity score at pre/post, paired comparisons and eta statistics. Performance-band counts are retained within that single outcome. Resim 1 (PDF p. 13) shows classroom photographs; Ek 1-3 (PDF pp. 22-24) show illustrative texts, with no additional scored outcomes. The basic-writing screening exercise and feasibility pilot on PDF p. 11 supplied selection/procedure information, not a separate reported AI-effect dataset; no pilot participant count or creative-outcome comparison is given, so one study is coded. Random assignment is at class level, not individual level; the author's quasi-experimental terminology is retained in the assignment explanation. The treatment combines AI examples with teacher instruction, peer feedback and rewriting that the control does not receive; the discussion explicitly says it cannot isolate ChatGPT from feedback in general (PDF p. 16, printed p. 85). No participant-level effect size or standard error has been derived, and the printed eta statistics are not treated as a standardized mean difference. No data/code repository or preregistration is stated.
